tasks.short: Read the treatment plan and recent notes, assist therapists in sessions and daily activities, report observations in the team meeting and write observations in the record.

steps.what: Psychiatric technician reads the treatment plan and recent notes before the shift
Psychiatric technician assists doctors, psychologists and rehabilitation therapists in working with patients
Psychiatric technician reports observations in the team meeting
Psychiatric technician writes observations in free text in the patient record

tasks.design: A shift view in the patient record ({OTHER}) shows each patient's current treatment goals and the last notes from the team on one screen. Observations are written in a short form per goal, so notes are easier to find for the team. Assisting therapists and reporting in the meeting stay with the technician; no recordings of patient conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans and notes were spread across the record and observations written as long free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient records offer shift views and goal-linked note forms.
tasks.still_hard: What matters about a patient often does not fit a form.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a patient is withdrawing before it shows in any score.

reach.learn: Whether goal-linked notes speed up reviews.

evidence.claim: Patient records offer shift views and note forms linked to treatment goals.
The medical dossier is kept 20 years and patients may ask who viewed it.

assumptions: Boundary: from the treatment plan to observation notes; treatment decisions are outside.
Input contract: goals set by the treating team in the record; fallback is reading all notes.
Assisting and reporting do not change.
No AI writes notes about patients.
research_questions: Do team members find observations faster?

incremental.description: Psychiatric technician learns the goal-linked form.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is with patients and the team.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree personal goals with the client, teach daily strategies in practice, make a day planner or cue cards and note progress on the goals.

steps.what: Psychiatric technician agrees personal goals with the client
Psychiatric technician teaches strategies to promote client wellness and independence
Psychiatric technician makes a day planner and cue cards for the client
Psychiatric technician notes progress on the client's goals

tasks.design: Day planners and cue cards start from templates with pictograms in the care record ({OTHER}) and are printed or shown on the client's tablet. Progress is noted per goal in a short form. Agreeing goals and teaching strategies stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Planners and cards were made by hand and progress written as free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Care records hold planner templates and goal-linked progress forms.
tasks.still_hard: Each client needs strategies that fit their own life.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the small step a client is willing to try today.

reach.learn: Whether shared templates align strategies across staff.

evidence.claim: Care records hold planner templates with pictograms and goal-linked progress forms.
Health data are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the treatment plan to progress notes; plan reviews are outside.
Input contract: goals agreed with the client; templates kept by the ward's senior technician; fallback is making cards by hand.
Agreeing and teaching do not change.
research_questions: Do clients use their planners more?

incremental.description: Psychiatric technician adds new pictograms to the templates.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is with the client.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk new staff through ward procedures, let them shadow shifts with feedback, point them to the procedures, sign off competences and practise de-escalation and safety rules.

steps.what: Psychiatric technician walks new employees through procedures to follow with psychiatric patients
Psychiatric technician lets new staff shadow shifts and gives feedback
Psychiatric technician hands out and explains the procedure binder
Psychiatric technician signs off competences on the paper induction list
Psychiatric technician practises de-escalation and safety rules with new staff

tasks.design: Ward procedures live in the learning system ({LMS}) with a short induction checklist, so new staff read them at their own pace. The technician signs off competences there instead of on paper. Walking through procedures, shadowing and practising de-escalation stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures were in a binder and competences signed on paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems hold procedures and induction checklists.
tasks.still_hard: Safe practice with patients is learned on the ward, not on screen.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a new colleague how to step back when a patient escalates.

reach.learn: Whether digital checklists show gaps earlier.

evidence.claim: Learning systems hold procedures and induction checklists with sign-off.
Records of employee competences can count as staff monitoring, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from a new employee's start to safety practised; formal appraisal is outside.
Input contract: procedures kept by the ward manager; fallback is the binder.
Walking through, shadowing and practising do not change.
New staff's reading time is outside the technician's savings.

incremental.description: Psychiatric technician checks new staff's reading progress.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is on the ward.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare each patient's medication, check patient, drug, dose and time, give it and watch it taken, record the administration and count controlled drug stock.

steps.what: Psychiatric technician issues medications from the dispensary per patient
Psychiatric technician checks patient, drug, dose and time before giving
Psychiatric technician gives the medication and watches it taken
Psychiatric technician signs the paper administration list to maintain records
Psychiatric technician counts controlled drug stock and writes it in the register

tasks.design: The pharmacy delivers medication in pouches per patient and time, so less preparing from the dispensary is needed. Scanning the patient's wristband and the pouch in the electronic administration record ({OTHER}) records the administration, and the controlled drug register lives in the same system for the count. Checking, giving and watching medication taken stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Medication was set out by hand from stock and signed for on paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Pharmacies supply pouches per patient, and electronic records take scanned administrations.
tasks.still_hard: As-needed medication and refusals need judgement and notes.
tasks.human_edge: Persuading a suspicious patient to take their medication without force.

reach.learn: Whether pouches cut ward stock errors.

evidence.claim: At Diakonessenhuis, robots fill medication rolls.
Dutch pharmacy systems run G-Standaard surveillance on interactions, contraindications and dose with KNMP minimum settings.
Reserved acts may be done by others only on assignment with instructions.

assumptions: Boundary: from medication orders to the stock register; prescribing is outside.
Input contract: orders from the psychiatrist in the record; pouches from the hospital pharmacy; fallback is preparing from stock and paper lists.
Checking and giving do not change.
Pharmacy staff time is outside the technician's savings.

incremental.description: Psychiatric technician handles scanner failures and missing pouches.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: As-needed doses and refusals stay manual.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The psychiatric technician keeps time with patients, teamwork, teaching and safe medication; searching notes, paper lists and binders shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technician who spends saved minutes on the ward floor with patients.
